items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: And Sarah Vaughan, she came with the band, and I started to writing music for her.

ctx.x: And he took her downtown and he bought her some dresses and things and talked to her mother and father and everything, and they let her go out on the road with us. So hence Sarah Vaughan. This was her first beginning with Earl Hines. And then, to our great discovery, she could play the piano, and she had played organ with the Newark Symphony Orchestra and studied with them, you know, when she was in high school. So when Earl find out this, he -- you know, he's an idea man -- right away he set up two pianos and…
Earl was a great show business man. He was looking for the flash. And Sarah Vaughan, she came with the band, and I started to writing music for her.

items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: I wrote for ... Sarah Vaughn ... And Sarah Vaughn, at one time she came into town and somebody was supposed to make the arrangements for a record date for her and they didn't even show up with the music. So she called me.

ctx.x: So now when we got out to California in 1940 we played at a place called Club Plantation, which is way out in Watts, you know, right straight out Central Avenue, right around into Watts. And in the show we had -- Sarah Vaughn was in the band too.
